functions.name: rtpp_shutdown
functions.description: Shuts down and cleans up an RTPproxy runtime/context represented by the opaque rtpp_cfg handle. Intended to gracefully terminate a previously initialized instance and release resources. Typical usage: obtain an rtpp_cfg* from rtpp_main(), run the service, then call rtpp_shutdown(cfg) during program teardown. Details of side effects and shutdown semantics are not documented in this header; behavior is inferred from the name and signature.
requirements: cfg must be a valid, initialized pointer to an RTPproxy context, typically one returned by rtpp_main(). (inferred)
cfg must not be NULL. (inferred from typical C API usage)
Do not call concurrently with other operations that use the same cfg; after shutdown, the cfg must not be used again. (inferred)
Call at most once for a given cfg to avoid double-shutdown or double-free scenarios. (inferred)
No ownership of cfg is transferred to the caller after shutdown; assume resources are released internally. (inferred)

functions.name: rtpp_main
functions.signature: struct rtpp_cfg *rtpp_main(int argc, const char * const *argv);
functions.description: Initializes the RTPproxy engine using command-line style arguments and returns an opaque runtime/context handle (rtpp_cfg*) for subsequent control (e.g., shutdown). Usage mirrors a conventional C main: pass argc and argv as provided by the environment; on success returns a non-NULL handle; on failure likely returns NULL (not documented here). No mutation of argv is implied by the const qualifiers.
requirements: argc should be >= 0. (inferred from conventional C signatures)
argv must point to an array of argc pointers to NUL-terminated C strings; each argv[i] must be non-NULL for i in [0, argc). (inferred)
argv may be NULL only when argc == 0. (inferred)
The returned pointer must be checked for NULL before use, as initialization may fail. (inferred from common C patterns)
The returned rtpp_cfg* is opaque; callers should not dereference or manipulate its internals and should pair it with rtpp_shutdown() to release resources. (inferred)
Call rtpp_main() before calling rtpp_shutdown() for the same process/context. (inferred)

data_types.description: An array of NUL-terminated C strings (argv) representing command-line style arguments passed with an accompanying argc count. Strings may include flags (e.g., -v), options, and values. For fuzzing, any printable bytes are acceptable as individual arguments as long as they contain no embedded NULs and are reasonably sized. argv may be NULL only when argc is 0.
